explanation: Preflight check passed (point is within threshold, pole-safety, Q2, beam-energy, and lookup-table coverage limits) and EXCLURAD ran to completion with exit code 0. It produced a valid Born cross section, sigma_born = 0.0008651649, and a valid leading-log approximation of delta (delta_ll = 0.796 for the polarized structure function, 0.885 unpolarized, from radcor.dat), but the full radiative-correction factor delta itself came out as NaN in both radtot.dat and radcor.dat (for both the unpolarized and polarized rows). The raw stdout shows one bremsstrahlung radiative-tail integration ('tai:') producing a NaN partial sum (visible as a stray 'tai:  NaN  0.1921E-03  10791  0' line with no bin indices) while all other tai bins at this point returned finite values; that single NaN corrupts the total used to form delta, even though it does not affect the independently-computed Born cross section. This reproduced identically on an independent smoke-test run of the same point, so it is a deterministic numerical failure of this specific kinematic point in the eta build rather than a transient issue. sigma_born is reported as computed; delta is reported as null because EXCLURAD itself did not produce a valid number for it.
